T: The party that saves the branch.
D: A branch manager throws an epic office Christmas party to save his staff from being sacked.
P: Serve the snacks when the snow machine douses the party and Walter.
S: Office party beef and onion sausage rolls
On the company card, before Carol's flight gets cancelled.

Flaky sausage rolls of beef and pork mince with caramelised onion and thyme, glazed with egg and sesame and served with tomato relish. Fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes until golden, then cool. Mix 300g beef mince and 200g pork mince with the onions, 1 tsp thyme, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 egg and salt. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each, roll and seal. Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with sesame and cut each into 4. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 200g tomato relish.
Mary's cheeseboard camembert, baked with honey
Hot camembert with rosemary and honey, toast, grapes and fig jam

A whole camembert baked with garlic, rosemary and honey until oozing, on a board with crusty bread, grapes and fig jam. Unwrap a 250g camembert, sit it back in its wooden box or a small dish and cut slits in the top. Push in slivers of 1 garlic clove and small rosemary sprigs and drizzle with 1 tbsp honey. Bake at 180C for 15 minutes until soft in the middle. Slice 1 baguette, brush with oil and toast 8 minutes. Serve the cheese hot on a board with the toasts, 300g grapes and 4 tbsp fig jam.
M: Clay's pitch to win over Walter Davis and Data City.

Little beef patties with melted cheddar, pickles, caramelised onion and burger sauce in soft brioche slider buns, eaten with one hand. Slowly fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp mustard and 1 tbsp chopped pickles. Roll 600g beef mince into 12 balls, smash flat in a very hot oiled pan, season and cook 2 minutes. Flip, add half a cheese slice each and cook 1 minute. Toast 12 brioche slider buns and fill with sauce, patty, onions and pickles.
Mary from HR's approved roast salmon
Mary from HR has signed off on it, and it is strictly non-denominational

Side of salmon roasted with honey mustard and dill, with crushed potatoes and green beans. Boil the potatoes for 18 minutes, drain and crush with the oil and salt. Mix the mustard, honey, lemon zest and half the chopped dill. Lay the salmon on a lined tray, spread with the glaze and roast at 200C for 15 minutes. Boil the beans for 4 minutes and toss with the butter. Scatter the salmon with the rest of the dill and serve with lemon wedges, potatoes and beans.
W: Vanilla cupcakes with red and green buttercream. Mary says no Cronuts.
Vanilla cupcakes with red and green buttercream, the Christmas colours the office goes all in on.
K: Egg custard nog with dark rum, brandy and nutmeg, for the eggnog luge

Homemade cooked eggnog with vanilla, cinnamon and fresh nutmeg, chilled and spiked with dark rum and brandy for the adults. Whisk 4 egg yolks with 100g caster sugar. Heat 600ml milk, 200ml cream, 1 cinnamon stick and 1 tsp vanilla until steaming. Slowly whisk into the yolks, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon, about 5 minutes. Strain and chill 2 hours. Stir in 60ml dark rum and 60ml brandy, or serve those on the side. Pour into glasses and grate fresh nutmeg over the top.

Mix the minces with the onions, thyme, breadcrumbs, one egg and salt.
Cut the pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each strip, roll and seal.

veg.n: Office party lentil, mushroom and onion rolls
veg.make_ahead: Make the lentil and mushroom filling up to 2 days ahead in the fridge; roll, glaze and bake on the day

ingredients.item: eggs (1 for the filling, 1 beaten for glazing)

steps.text: Fry the onions in the butter until golden.
Add the mushrooms and cook until all the liquid has gone, then cool.
Lightly mash the lentils and mix with the onion and mushroom, soy sauce, thyme, breadcrumbs, one egg and salt.
Cut the pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each strip, roll and seal.
Brush with egg, sprinkle with sesame and cut into pieces.
Bake at 200C until golden. Serve with relish.
